description: Gossypium hirsutum (upland cotton): a shrubby annual with lobed leaves, cream flowers that turn pink, and bolls of white lint.

diseases.name: Bacterial Blight (Angular Leaf Spot)
diseases.description: A bacterial disease of cotton that spots the leaves, blackens the stems ('black arm') and rots the bolls.
diseases.causes: The bacteria come in on seed and crop debris and spread by wind-driven rain, splash and overhead irrigation in warm, humid weather.
symptoms: Small, water-soaked, angular spots between the leaf veins
Spots turn brown to black; leaves yellow and fall
Black, sunken lesions on stems and on the bolls
diseases.effect: Leaf loss and boll rot reduce yield and lint quality.
diseases.untreated: In wet seasons it defoliates plants and rots many bolls.

steps.title: Remove badly spotted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off badly spotted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer bacteria are left to splash onto healthy leaves.

steps.title: Avoid overhead irrigation
steps.instruction: Water in furrows or by drip, and keep out of the crop while it is wet.
steps.rationale: Splash and wet leaves spread the bacteria.

steps.title: Copper spray where advised
steps.instruction: Spray a registered copper product following the label.
steps.rationale: Protects new leaves; it cannot cure existing spots.

prevention.title: Sow acid-delinted or treated seed of resistant varieties
Plough in or remove crop debris
prevention.detail: Debris carries it to the next crop.

lifecycle: Bacteria survive on seed and crop debris.
Rain splash carries them to the leaves.
They enter through pores and wounds; angular spots form.
Spots on stems and bolls spread it further.

diseases.name: Cotton Leaf Curl Disease
diseases.pathogen: Cotton leaf curl virus complex (begomoviruses with betasatellite)
diseases.description: A whitefly-borne virus disease of cotton in South Asia and Africa: leaves curl, veins thicken and plants are stunted.
diseases.causes: Whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) carry the virus from infected cotton, weeds and other hosts as they feed.
symptoms: Leaves curl upward or downward, cupped and crinkled
Veins on the underside thicken and darken, often with leaf-like outgrowths (enations)
Plants stunted, with few, small bolls
diseases.untreated: Early infection can make a whole field uneconomic.

steps.title: Remove infected plants early
steps.instruction: Pull out curled, stunted plants and destroy them.
steps.rationale: Each one is a source for whiteflies.

steps.title: Keep whiteflies down
steps.instruction: Monitor with yellow sticky traps and use controls registered locally, following the label.

steps.title: Clear weed hosts
steps.instruction: Remove weeds and volunteer cotton round the field.
steps.rationale: They harbour the virus and whiteflies.

lifecycle: Whiteflies pick up the virus from infected plants and weeds.
They carry it to healthy cotton.
New leaves curl and veins thicken.
Plants are stunted and set few bolls.

diseases.name: Fusarium Wilt
diseases.description: A soil-borne fungal wilt of cotton that blocks the water vessels; worst in sandy soils with root-knot nematodes.
diseases.causes: The fungus lives in the soil for years and enters through the roots, often through nematode wounds; it spreads in soil, water and seed.
symptoms: Leaves yellow and wilt, starting at the margins and lower leaves
Leaves dry and fall; plants wilt in the heat of the day
Brown streaks inside the stem when it is cut
diseases.effect: Plants are stunted and lose their leaves and bolls.
diseases.untreated: Seedlings and young plants die; the soil stays infested for years.

steps.title: Confirm by cutting the stem
steps.instruction: Cut a wilted stem near the soil and look for brown streaks inside.
steps.rationale: Separates wilt from drought or root rot.

steps.title: Remove dead plants
steps.instruction: Pull out and destroy dead plants with their roots.
steps.rationale: They release spores into the soil.

steps.title: Balance the soil
steps.instruction: Keep potassium up and manage root-knot nematodes as advised.
steps.rationale: Healthy roots and fewer nematode wounds slow the wilt.

prevention.title: Rotate with non-host crops
prevention.detail: Cereals lower the fungus and the nematodes.

lifecycle: The fungus lives in the soil for years.
It enters the roots, often through nematode wounds.
Leaves yellow and wilt; the plant may die.
conditions: Sandy, acid soils low in potassium.
